claim: a 22M encoder trained on planted indirect injections with matched twins beats the accessible 184M baseline on indirect and pasted injection at CPU latency; direct attacks are where it still loses
verdict: v10-multilingual: clears the baseline on 8 of 10 headline slices; loses on ['multilingual_direct']
verdict_rule: a slice is cleared when the Wilson 95% intervals of correctness at the run's threshold are apart; three seeds per round, spread reported

protectai-v2.note: Served baseline, ProtectAI deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2 (184M, Apache-2.0) at its shipped 0.5. Prompt Guard 2 is gated (403 with this account). Misses are the planted carriers: AUROC 0.50 on indirect in-dist, 0.41 on hard; flags 43 of 100 NotInject sentences.

v1-templates.note:
Changed: MiniLM-L6 fine-tuned on planted carriers, 9,183 rows, no matched negatives, 50 benign user turns against 2,000 attack ones.
Moved: NotInject 57 to 0 points; deepset 76 to 0; the threshold at 1% benign FPR on carriers was 0.0008, so every user turn was flagged.
Why: short text was the label; the carrier template, not the payload, separated the classes (AUROC 1.00 on in-dist and held-out carriers).
Learned: a generator's own negatives are not negatives; the model learned the generator. A 22M encoder finds the shortcut in 19 seconds.
Reproduce: seed 1, tests t-fcaff01e and t-693f5a0b, python run.py (v1 data shape is in the README's first round).

v3-twins-dedupe.note:
Changed: every planted row gets a twin with the same carrier, position and framing and a harmless insert; 108 payloads sharing an 8-gram with the frozen test dropped (training payloads are Gandalf strings); 3,500 oasst1 benign user turns; threshold from a validation split of train at 1% FPR.
Moved: NotInject 57 to 97 points, sim_tool 42 to 84, held-out families 18 to 55, hard 55 to 63; deepset 76 to 67, DOWN.
Why: the twins take the carrier and the length out of the label; what is left is the insert. deepset is direct German and English attacks the training never covers (length-only LR gets 0.80 AUROC there).
Learned: matched negatives are the whole game for a planted-data classifier; the payload-removed score falls to 0.002 on every probe pair, the twin FPR is 0, and the miss is recall on unseen families (pair accuracy 53 to 62 points).
Reproduce: seeds 1,2,3 (spread 0.8 points on the full test), tests t-fcaff01e and t-693f5a0b, python run.py

v4-spml-direct.note:
Changed: added SPML (MIT, 16k rows): 3,470 direct injections and 3,470 benign asks as user turns, and 8,079 of its injection prompts as planted payloads with length-matched benign twins. 25,461 rows.
Moved: deepset 67 to 69 points (AUROC 0.69/0.71/0.80 over seeds, baseline 0.88); NotInject 97 to 82; hard 62 to 52; sim_tool 84 to 78. DOWN on three of five headline slices.
Why: SPML "injections" are long role-play prompts ("You are HealthAI, a virtual consultant...") and its benign side is short asks, so length and prompt-likeness re-entered the label; NotInject's trigger-word sentences and the hard twins pay for it. Pair accuracy on held-out families fell to 48 to 52 points.
Learned: a public set labelled "prompt injection" is not the behaviour this classifier is for; SPML is mostly jailbreak-shaped role play, which the scope excludes. Volume from the wrong distribution moves the headline the wrong way; the round is kept on the page as the negative result it is.
Reproduce: seeds 1,2,3; tests t-fcaff01e, t-693f5a0b, t-371b20a4; python data.py --sim sim_rows.jsonl (SPML on by default), modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v4.jsonl --tag v4-spml --seeds 1,2,3

v5-channels.note:
Changed: SPML out; two channels in. Copy-paste: 1,200 matched pairs where the carrier is pasted under a user ask. Six-domain agent traffic from wai.simulate (clinic, bank, e-commerce, legal, devops, travel; stance pinned; 384 rows) harvested as tool-result and agent-reply carriers, half planted. 15,588 rows.
Moved: sim_tool 84 to 92 points (AUROC 0.99 over seeds); held-out family 55 to 64; paste 60 to 64; NotInject 97 to 93; hard 62 to 60 (inside the 5-point noise band); deepset 67 to 69 (AUROC 0.71 to 0.73, baseline 0.88, still a loss).
Why: the pasted channel is what moved paste (the model had never seen a carrier under an ask); the domain traffic is what moved sim_tool, which is that traffic's frozen cousin. Hard did not move because its transforms (zero-width, split, deep) are absent from training by design.
Learned: channel coverage beats volume: 3,500 rows of the right shape moved three slices up, 13,000 rows of SPML moved three down. Twin FPR rose to 0.01 to 0.025 as the twins got harder; pair accuracy stayed at 56 to 62.
Reproduce: seeds 1,2,3; tests t-fcaff01e, t-693f5a0b, t-371b20a4; python data.py --sim sim_rows.jsonl --sim-extra sim_domains.jsonl --no-spml; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v5.jsonl --tag v5-channels --seeds 1,2,3

v6-twin-margin.note:
Changed: same rows as v5, plus a pairwise hinge on every matched twin, max(0, 2.0 - (s_pos - s_twin)), lambda 1.0, the preference-loss analogue on the pair (Lambert 2025, chapter Direct Alignment). Pairs batched together so both members share a step.
Moved: hard 60 to 54 points, held-out family 64 to 58, paste 64 to 61, sim_tool 92 to 90; deepset 69 flat; NotInject 93 to 94. Pair accuracy 55 to 58 against v5's 56 to 62: the loss aimed at pairs did not raise pair accuracy.
Why: the margin is paid on the training pairs, which the cross-entropy already separates (1.4% of training rows sit in the uncertain band by round 5), so the extra term pushes the logit scale rather than the decision on unseen families; the threshold moved to 0.96 to 0.99.
Learned: a pairwise term on pairs the model already gets right buys nothing: the book's within-group-contrast rule applied to a classifier. The gradient lives where the pair is mixed, and by round 5 the training pairs are not. New carriers, not a new loss, is the next round.
Reproduce: seeds 1,2,3; same tests; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v5.jsonl --tag v6-twin --loss twin --margin 2.0 --seeds 1,2,3

v7-llm-carriers.note:
Changed: no template carrier. wai.simulate with haiku as situation writer, user and world (execute= writes each tool result as the document that tool returns), six businesses, 384 rollouts, 579 documents plus the agents' drafts and 830 asks; public payloads and 125 checker-confirmed paraphrases; 270 checker-confirmed benign inserts; matched twins. 10,851 rows.
Moved: llm (legal documents) 67 to 73 points, AUROC 0.71 to 0.83 with 0 false positives (baseline 49, AUROC 0.50); sim_tool 92 to 89; NotInject 93 flat; deepset 69 flat; hard 60 to 41 and paste 64 to 47, DOWN; held-out family 64 to 41, DOWN.
Why: the validation split is now model-written carriers with model-written inserts, so the 1% FPR threshold landed at 0.11 to 0.18 and the template-carrier tests (hard, paste, held-out family) pay in false positives; this round never saw a template carrier and does not transfer to them. This round also trained on legal traffic, so its llm number is in-distribution; v7b holds legal out.
Learned: the bag-of-words probe on the indirect slices fell from 0.82 to 0.63 AUROC when the carriers changed hands from the template to the model: the shortcut left the data. What the model then learns transfers to model-written documents and not to the template ones, which is the same finding from the other side; the union (v8) is the next round.
Reproduce: seeds 1,2,3; tests t-fcaff01e, t-693f5a0b, t-371b20a4, t-157cf4ee; sim_llm.py per business; gen_inserts.py; python data_llm.py --tag v7; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v7.jsonl --tag v7-llm --seeds 1,2,3

v7-mined-weights.note:
Changed: v5 rows scored by v5 seed 1; the 214 rows in the uncertain band (116 wrong) weighted x3, the rest 1.0; retrained. The rejection-sampling idea (keep what the model finds hard) applied to a classifier, with the random-weight control beside it.
Moved: over three seeds, hard 59 to 56, paste 64 to 62, sim_tool 92 to 93, NotInject 94 to 93, held-out family 63 to 62, deepset 69 to 68; every move inside the seed spread (0.8 to 2.6 points). The random-weight control: hard 58, paste 62, sim_tool 92, NotInject 93, family 63.
Why: 214 of 15,588 rows sit in the band, 1.4%; tripling their weight moves 4% of the loss mass. The pool is saturated for this model; there is nothing to mine.
Learned: mining against a random-weight control is the way to know whether the pool has anything left, and here it did not; the two arms are one arm. New carriers (v7, v8) are where the misses are, not re-weighted old ones.
Reproduce: python mine.py --model out/v5-channels-seed1 --train out/train_v5.jsonl --tag v7mine; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v7mine.jsonl --tag v7mine --weight-key weight --seeds 1,2,3

v7-random-weights-control.note:
Changed: the control for mining: the same 214 x3 weights placed on rows drawn at random (seed 0), the same training. Everything else as v5.
Moved: hard 58, paste 62, deepset 69, sim_tool 92, NotInject 93, held-out family 63: v5 within the seed spread on every slice, and the mined arm within the seed spread of this one.
Why: 4% of the loss mass moved to random rows is a small learning-rate change, and the pool is saturated either way.
Learned: a control that cannot fail reads as coverage; this one could have (a x3 on random rows can hurt), and it came out flat, so the mined arm's flat result is a property of the pool and not of the weighting.
Reproduce: mine.py writes out/train_v7mine-random.jsonl beside the mined file; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v7mine-random.jsonl --tag v7mine-random --weight-key weight --seeds 1,2,3

v7b-llm-heldout-domain.note:
Changed: v7's data with the legal business held out of training (its 211 documents become test_llm, t-157cf4ee, with held-out families planted and model-written inserts). 9,972 rows. The fair version of v7's llm number.
Moved: llm 49 to 73/80/73 points over seeds (AUROC 0.83 to 0.89, 0 to 2 false positives in 211), against v5's 62 to 67 and the baseline's 49; sim_tool 93, NotInject 92 to 96; hard 46 and paste 49, DOWN from v5's 59 and 64; held-out family 42 to 54, DOWN; deepset 68 flat.
Why: a model that has never seen a template carrier scores the template tests as out of distribution, and its threshold (0.11 to 0.18 from the model-written validation split) is a long way from where the template twins separate. The llm gain holds on a business it never saw, so it is a transfer to documents, not to a business.
Learned: the two carrier families do not transfer to each other in either direction: template-trained v5 gets 62 to 67 on model-written documents, model-trained v7b gets 46 to 49 on template tests. A classifier trained on one generator scores that generator. The union is the next round.
Reproduce: python data_llm.py --tag v7b --holdout-domain legal; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v7b.jsonl --tag v7b-llm --seeds 1,2,3; same tests plus t-157cf4ee

v8-union.note:
Changed: v5's rows (template twins, paste channel, six-domain traffic) plus v7b's rows (model-written carriers, legal held out), 23,960 rows, 6,260 matched pairs; validation split from the union.
Moved: llm 49 to 73/76/72 points (AUROC 0.79 to 0.81); hard 51 to 56, paste 55 to 61, held-out family 56 to 64: between v5 and v7b on each; sim_tool 93 to 95, NotInject 93 to 95; deepset 69 to 70, still 6 points under the 184M baseline.
Why: the union sees both carrier families, so both thresholds' worlds are in the validation split and the 1% FPR point (0.19 to 0.32) sits between them; the template tests give back most of what v7b lost and the llm test keeps most of what v7b gained. Pair accuracy on held-out families 53 to 56, twin FPR 0.045 to 0.06.
Learned: by the pre-stated rule (sum of headline points, seed 1) v5 stays the pick at 509 against 491: v8 buys 6 points on the held-out business and pays 9 on hard, 9 on paste and 8 on the held-out families, all template-carrier tests. On the slices no template wrote (llm, sim_tool, NotInject) v8 is the better arm; on deepset both lose, on every seed, and that is the number to fix next with a non-Gandalf direct set. Seed spread 1.0 to 3.7 points, inside the 5.1 noise band.
Reproduce: python data_llm.py --tag v8 --holdout-domain legal --merge out/train_v5.jsonl; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v8.jsonl --tag v8-union --seeds 1,2,3; tests t-fcaff01e, t-693f5a0b, t-371b20a4, t-157cf4ee

v9-seeded-world.note:
Changed: v8's rows plus 485 tool results from three seeded wai.simulate runs (bank, travel, e-commerce): the seeds are AgentDojo's own user tasks and InjecAgent's user cases, a model writes each tool result, and the world (execute=) plants a public training-family payload into half of them and records it, so the label comes from the world, not from a planting pass afterwards. 24,406 rows.
Moved: AgentDojo documents 67 to 74/82/78 points over seeds (external, AUROC in results.json); held-out business 73 to 78/78/79; hard 51 to 54/58/61; paste 55 to 58/62/62; sim_tool 93 to 98; held-out family 56 to 67/64/58; NotInject 94 to 93/96/95; LLMail recall 40 to 44/36/45; deepset 69 flat; multilingual 20 flat.
Why: the seeded asks are the benchmark's own situations, so the tool results the world returns are the documents an injection benchmark reads (calendar events, transactions, hotel pages), and planting inside the world keeps the carrier and the payload in one register. That is the AgentDojo slice moving 15 points on documents the recipe never saw.
Learned: seeds= plus execute= is the SDK's way to make a labelled classifier set for an agent benchmark: the benchmark's asks in, the world's documents out, the label known by construction. It did nothing for direct attacks in other languages, which no English carrier can teach.
Reproduce: sim_seeds.py per business (96 rollouts each); python data_llm.py --tag v9 --holdout-domain legal --merge out/train_v5.jsonl --seeded sim_seeds_*.jsonl; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v9.jsonl --tag v9-seeded --seeds 1,2,3; tests t-fcaff01e, t-693f5a0b, t-371b20a4, t-157cf4ee, t-109345aa

v10-multilingual.note:
Changed: v9's rows plus 298 model translations of public attack strings and 322 of benign statements (German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian; a checker dropped 430 that lost or gained an instruction), as user turns and as 586 planted twins; base model microsoft/Multilingual-MiniLM-L12-H384 (MIT, XLM-R vocabulary, 21.4M non-embedding parameters). 26,082 rows.
Moved: multilingual direct recall 20 to 45/45/36 (baseline 98); deepset 69 to 70/73/72 (baseline 76, still a loss); held-out business 78 to 84/81/77; hard 58 to 62/64/57; paste 61 to 63/68/58; sim_tool 98 to 97/100/98; held-out family 63 to 69/68/64; AgentDojo documents 78 to 85/68/62 (n=100, seed spread 23 points); LLMail 42 to 43/50/36.
Why: an English uncased WordPiece model maps a German attack to [UNK] fragments; the XLM-R vocabulary reads it. 300 translated attacks doubled multilingual recall and did not close the gap to a model trained on multilingual injection data at scale.
Learned: the multilingual direction works and costs the budget: 118 MB int8 against the 60 MB target (the 250k-row embedding table is 96M of the 117M parameters) and 15/36/90 ms at 128/256/512 tokens against 7.5/17/44. Within the budget v9 is the pick; the next multilingual round needs a pruned vocabulary or a distilled small multilingual encoder, not more translations.
Reproduce: gen_translate.py translations.json; python data_llm.py --tag v10 --holdout-domain legal --merge out/train_v5.jsonl --seeded sim_seeds_*.jsonl --translations translations.json; modal run train_modal.py --train-file out/train_v10.jsonl --tag v10-multilingual --base-model microsoft/Multilingual-MiniLM-L12-H384 --seeds 1,2,3

  before the GPU: size the held-out test (holdout_size) and measure its noise over three runs (eval_variance); decontaminate the pool against it; train a random selection of the same size beside the real one; keep one chat template across stages and mask tool turns out of the loss (loss_mask); check over-refusal on a benign set (refusal_report); and with beta=0, watch the drift from the reference (mean_kl) (Lambert 2025, chapters Instruction Fine-Tuning, Tool Use, Over-Optimization, Regularization, Evaluation)
  not routed: rm (where a program grades, the program is the reward); Async and its correction (wrap the routed method when the sampler lags the policy); OPD's divergence and top_k and OPSD's anchor (not decidable from rows; the docstrings give the defaults' sources); Swarm (a rollout rule, not a trainer; gate it on Swarm.calibration); learning rate, clip and KL (see the method's docstring); the band per stance or difficulty (a pool mixed overall can floor on one slice: route each slice)
